# mmf-mage — a Gnome Mage on seed 1: what the staircases cost and what a mage cannot buy

*Run `mmf-mage` and its continuation `mmf-mage.2` (see "The machine restarted"
below). Seed 1, Gnome Mage, build `e473720ed88a` (`g9afcd64-dirty`).
145 decisions, turn 4872, ended alive on depth 1 with 8 of 8 hit points,
2 of 2 spell points, 7 gold, AC 17. Deepest level reached: depth 3.
Character level 1. Kills: 0. Experience: 0.*

---

## 1. What happened

The character was born a Gnome Mage with 8 hit points (race die 8, class
die 0, constitution -1 so no bonus), 2 spell points, and a to-hit of 9 with
the kit rapier and 11 with a thrown flask. Its constitution is -1 (the
Gnome's +1 and the Mage's -2), so every level it gains about half a hit
point less than a character with a constitution of 0 would.

**The plan was:** buy the escapers and the oil in the town, then go down as
fast as the level allows, casting *Find Traps, Doors & Stairs* once per
fresh level to find the staircase, and kill whatever pays experience on
the way. The plan failed at its last step and nowhere else.

* **Asks 1-10** — birth. The race menu's Gnome is `e`, the class menu's
  Mage is `b`; the menu's letters skip `h`, `j`, `k` and `l`, so the
  rows have to be read off the screen. The town puts the character on the
  down staircase before it has walked anywhere: the status line says
  *Down staircase* on the first screen and `>` goes straight to depth 1.
* **Asks 11-31** — the first shopping trip. 325 gold, spent on 20 flasks
  of oil (60), 3 rations (9), a Studded Leather Armour (150), a Robe (36)
  and a set of Gauntlets (24). The Armoury of this seed has **no helms at
  all** — only robes, soft and scale armour, gloves, gauntlets and boots
  — so the shopping list in my own playbook does not exist here. The
  Robe and the Studded Leather Armour are both `soft armor` and share the
  body slot, so only the Studded can be worn: the Robe (36 gold) is
  dead money. Worn armour: AC 15.
* **Asks 32-83** — depth 1, then depth 2, then depth 3 and back.
  *Find Traps, Doors & Stairs* was studied at birth (ask 14) instead of
  *Magic Missile*, deliberately: at character level 1 the whole
  experience economy of the game is decided by how many kills can be
  found, and *Magic Missile* does not help with finding them. The first
  cast (ask 34) **failed silently**: the character sheet afterwards
  showed `Cur Exp 0`, and the spell pays 2 experience on its first
  success, so the cast had failed its 12 per cent roll, and the screen
  showed no message at all. The second cast (ask 47, on depth 1) worked
  and revealed **two down staircases**; `l>g` reached the first in two
  walks (3 tiles, then 3 tiles) and the level 2 chamber beyond it held
  three sleeping cave spiders (7 hp, AC 19, 1d4, speed 120, so two
  blows a turn) and a sleeping blue yeek.
* **Asks 53-55** — the decision that shaped the run: **I left that
  chamber without fighting.** The yeek was one wake-event from waking
  (its sleep is 10, and `monster_reduce_sleep` removes `100/local_noise`
  a time, so any monster within ten tiles loses its sleep in one roll),
  oil against its AC 16 is a 12 per cent shot that needs about eight
  throws, and eight throws of a 1d5 monster at AC 17 is about 22 damage
  against my 8 hit points. The three spiders next to it would have woken
  with it. So I went up.
* **Asks 84-110** — the town trip, which cost 26 decisions and bought
  the run its safety: a Cloak (6), 4 more flasks of oil (12), a second
  Potion of Cure Light Wounds (20) and a second Scroll of Phase Door
  (15). AC 17. The unknown *Purple Speckled Potion* was identified by
  **giving it to the Alchemist** (the store's `s` command learns the kind
  even with selling off): it was a **Potion of Boldness**, whose effect
  is `CURE:AFRAID` — of no use to a mage. The way home from depth 2 was
  the **Scroll of Word of Recall** (read it in the dungeon and it takes
  you to the town after 15 to 34 player actions; a rest of 61 actions
  covers the longest wait), because the staircases are paired the wrong
  way round: `<` ascends only from an *up* staircase and lands you on a
  *down* staircase of the level above, so depth 2's up staircase leads
  to depth 1's down staircase, which needs a second up staircase to
  reach the town.
* **Asks 111-145** — a fresh depth 1, a third cast of *Find Traps* (two
  more down staircases found), and then the walking problem: **the game's
  own pathfinder could not take me to the staircase.** `l>g` moved one
  tile and stopped, twice. The reason is in `find_path`
  (`player-path.c`): `only_known = square_isknown(start) &&
  square_isknown(dest)`, so with a known destination but unknown ground
  in between there is no path over remembered ground and the walk is one
  or two tiles. Plain digit strings walk the whole way but stop at the
  first wall. I spent the last 30 decisions walking corridors by digit
  strings and found **no monster at all**, and the level ends with the
  character at 8 of 8 hit points, 2 of 2 spell points, 7 gold and a
  pack of 24 flasks of oil, 4 Potions of Cure Light Wounds, 2 Scrolls of
  Phase Door, 4 rations and a book of spells.

The run's one real piece of luck: the flask I picked up in the big room
on depth 1 was **a Potion of Cure Light Wounds** (a 25 per cent draw
from the depth 1 potion pool), so the unidentified potion became a
third heal rather than a gamble.

## 2. The decisions I would take back

1. **Six decisions went to keys that were eaten by menus.** `C` (the
   character sheet) is a menu: my `mc` meant "change name" and opened
   the rename prompt. `[` (the monster list) leaves a "press any key"
   prompt that ate my `<`. The store list eats keys: a ten-key route
   sent while the Armoury was still on screen lost nine of them, and the
   tenth (`2`) was read as movement into the shop's wall. The cast
   prompt needs two decisions (`ma` then `c`), because the spell list
   takes a key of its own. Each of these cost a turn and an ask. The
   rule that would have saved them is in my own playbook already —
   **one command per ask, and `C`/`[`/the store need an Escape first** —
   and I broke it four times.
2. **I spent four decisions trying the aimed walk** (`*` + digits + `g`,
   the recipe the shared `aim.py` tool prints) in the town, where it
   cannot work: `*` opens the target mode with the cursor on my own
   square, my square was the down staircase, and `aux_terrain` consumes
   a key to describe an interesting square and ends the mode on the
   next one. `Target Aborted` is printed after a *successful* pathfind
   too, because `target_is_set()` is false after `CMD_PATHFIND`, so
   that message says nothing about whether the walk happened.
3. **The 26 decisions of the town trip were worth it, but I made them
   with 0 spell points.** The order that cost me: I left depth 2 with an
   empty bar, spent the next 26 decisions buying things and resting, and
   came back down with 2 spell points and a character I could survive.
   The cheaper order would have been to spend the first bar of spell
   points on a cast *before* the trip (depth 2's staircase was already
   known at that moment), and to use the town trip to buy oil rather
   than armour: AC 15 to 17 is worth about 2 per cent of hits, while
   the flasks are the only attack a CL1 mage has.
4. **I never went below depth 3 and I never killed anything.** Both
   follow from the same measurement, below: at character level 1 on
   depth 1 a kill pays 1 to 5 experience, CL2 needs 12, and the level
   holds about fifty monsters on 13,068 squares. **A CL1 mage needs
   three to five kills, and a kill costs thirty to sixty decisions to
   find.** That is the real reason this run ends at level 1 with no
   kills, and no shopping list and no spell changes it.

## 3. Where the manual was wrong, or not enough

* **`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §8 and my own playbook both say the
  aimed cursor plus `g` walks 17 to 44 tiles in one ask.** That is true
  over *remembered* ground. On a level you have just entered there is
  none, and the walk is one to three tiles: `l>g` moved me 3, 3, 12
  and 1 tiles on four different levels, and the aimed walk one tile.
  The manual's own advice ("aim at a landmark you have lit") is right,
  but it never says that this is also true of `l>g` to a *known*
  staircase, which is the case the manual presents as the solution.
* **The manual's "one cast of Find Traps finds the staircase" is right
  and the "six casts on a six-position grid" plan in my own MAGE.md is
  wrong**, but for a reason neither states: on a fresh level the
  detection spell's window is 45 by 81 squares, and my first cast found
  **no doors and no stairs at all** in a window that contained the up
  staircase I was standing next to — because the cast had failed.
  A failed cast prints no message in this build, so the only way to
  know a cast did anything is to look at `Cur Exp` on the character
  sheet afterwards. The manual says a spell's first use pays
  experience; it does not say that the *absence* of experience means the
  cast failed.
* **`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §6b says an unknown scroll or potion can
  be identified by "giving it to the store that buys that type".** In
  this build that needs the store's `s` command, which is not on the
  store's printed menu, so it looks as if the trick does not exist. It
  does: `s` opens a "Give which item?" prompt, and the kind is learned
  even though the shop pays nothing.
* **The manual's depth 1 potion pool is right (84 per cent harmless,
  measured from the object's own `alloc` weights) but it does not say
  that the pool differs by depth**: the depth 1 pool is eleven kinds
  (Cure Light Wounds 80, Neutralize Poison 60, Speed, Heroism and
  Boldness 40 each, Slime Mold Juice 10, and Sleep, Blindness,
  Confusion, Poison and Slowness 10 each), while the *scroll* pool on
  depth 1 is Treasure Detection, Light, Phase Door, Detect Invisible and
  Blessing 50 each against Deep Descent 20, Summon Monster 10 and
  Darkness 10 — **40 of the 290 scroll weight on depth 1 is dangerous (14 per cent),
  and the first use pays the kind's own level, so a scroll's expected
  experience is about 0.2.** I left the scroll on the floor; that was
  the right call and the numbers say so.
* **The manual's claim that "the shops restock daily" is true in
  general but did not happen inside my game day.** My second visit to
  the Armoury showed exactly the first list minus what I had bought
  (the Studded Leather Armour gone, the gloves 16 to 15, the Gauntlets
  6 to 5). I wrote in my notebook at the time that the stock had
  rotated; that was wrong, and I have corrected it in the notebook.

## 4. What I could not see, or could not do

* **I never found a monster to kill in 145 decisions.** So this run
  measures nothing about the experience formula, about how much damage
  a CL1 mage's oil actually does, or about how a mage dies; my family's
  earlier measurement of the mage's early game (minimaxflash-2: 158
  asks, depth 1, level 1, 4 experience) stands, and this run matches it.
* **I could not walk to a staircase the game had told me about.** The
  staircase on depth 1 was 12 tiles west and 15 north of me and the
  pathfinder could not do it; I walked it by hand in pieces and ran out
  of decisions. The M map showed me both staircases and both doors, and
  the doors were the more useful of the two, because a door is a map of
  where the rooms are.
* **I could not tell a helm from a pair of boots on a text screen.**
  The `]` glyph is used by both (`object.txt`: the Iron Shod Boots are
  `graphics:]:U`, the Metal Cap is `graphics:]:s`), and I picked up a
  pair of Leather Sandals expecting a helm.
* **The town's own staircase is the only way down from the town, and
  the status line is the only place it appears**: the tile under `@` is
  never drawn, so the map never shows the `>` you are standing on.

## 5. Leads

1. **A CL1 mage's experience problem is a *finding* problem, not a
   fighting problem, and on depth 1 it cannot be solved at all.**
   *Evidence:* `classic_gen` places `level_monster_min + randint1(8) + k`
   monsters (about fifty) on 198x66 squares, and `pick_and_place_distant_monster`
   is called with `dis = 0`, so they are placed at any distance from the
   up staircase and start asleep; a kill at CL1 on depth 1 pays 1 to 5
   experience (`monster.txt`: the small kobold is 5, the soldier ant 3,
   the grey mould 3) and CL2 needs 12 for a Gnome. **What would settle
   it:** one run that counts the decisions per kill on depth 1 and
   again on depth 2, and says whether the depth 2 doubling (a giant
   green frog is 6 experience on depth 1 and 12 on depth 2) is enough
   to pay for the level it costs to get there.
2. **The detection spell is worth more for its doors than for its
   stairs.** *Evidence:* the spell's window is 45 by 81 squares and it
   reported "You sense the presence of doors!" on all three of my
   successful casts, and the M map then drew the doors at box (5,13),
   (9,14) and (21,18); a room is a hundred squares of concentrated
   search, a corridor ten. **What would settle it:** a run that counts
   monsters per room visited against monsters per corridor length
   swept, with the doors marked from a cast.
3. **A failed detection cast is invisible, and the only test is the
   experience counter.** *Evidence:* ask 34's cast left `Cur Exp 0` and
   an empty message line, while a success pays 2 (`class.txt`: the
   spell's last field is 2) and prints "You sense ...". **What would
   settle it:** the same cast twice in a row on the same level, with the
   character sheet read after each, to see whether the second cast
   succeeds and whether a failure ever prints anything.
4. **The staircases are paired so that ascending takes two up
   staircases to leave a level for the town**, and the Scroll of Word
   of Recall is the cheap way home. *Evidence:* `<` did nothing at all
   from a down staircase (the turn counter did not move) and landed me
   on a down staircase when I used it from an up one; the Recall took
   610 game turns of rest to fire and cost two decisions. **What would
   settle it:** whether the Recall's timer is shorter when read after
   a long rest (the countdown ticks once every ten game turns whatever
   you do).
5. **A CL1 mage has no answer to armoured monsters, and the armour he
   wears costs him his throw.** *Evidence:* `calc_bonuses` adds a worn
   item's to-hit to `state->to_h` for everything that is not a weapon
   or a bow, and `chance_of_missile_hit_base` adds `state->to_h` to the
   throw for a `THROWING` item (a flask of oil has the flag), so the
   Studded Leather Armour's (-1) takes my oil from 11 to 10 and the
   hit rate against an AC 14 target from 27 to 20 per cent. **What
   would settle it:** a mage wearing no armour at all against the same
   target, at the same range, in the same level, so that the armour's
   cost is measured rather than computed.
6. **The store's `s` command identifies a kind for nothing, and that
   is worth a trip.** *Evidence:* the Purple Speckled Potion became a
   Potion of Boldness (`CURE:AFRAID`) with no gold and no further use
   to me. **What would settle it:** whether the same trick identifies a
   scroll, since a scroll's kind is what decides whether it is a Deep
   Descent.

## 6. The machine restarted

At ask 39 the host rebooted and the game process died with it; the
runner said "no new question within 60s" and the run was left
"stopped, saved". The documented way on is `borg_runner carry-on`, which
**replays the old keys into a fresh process**: the run continued as
`mmf-mage.2`, the tool printed `identical: true` (the replay
reproduced my game exactly), it left the game waiting at ask 40, turn
1131 with my notebook inherited, and it even re-ran the `.6` I had
queued when the machine died. The two runs are one character and one
line of play; the name changed only because the process had to change.
